newsitem.title: INDIA: India seeks to increase trade with Latin America.
newsitem.headline: India seeks to increase trade with Latin America.

text.p: India keenly wants to tap new markets in Latin America as it seeks to boost trade with countries outside its traditional areas of business, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on Wednesday.
Ramaiah told a group of Latin American ambassadors and Indian business leaders that two-way trade had picked up smartly after his country launched free-market reforms in 1991.
India's trade with Latin American countries rose 160 percent from 12.0 billion rupees in 1990/91 (April-March) to 31.4 billion in 1995/96 (April-March), industry officials said.

"We are willing to provide all the help that we are capable of to improve bilateral trade with the Latin American countries," said Ramaiah, speaking at a seminar organised by leading Indian industry bodies.
Towards this end, he said, India would set up warehouse facilities for its exporters to Latin America as well as take steps to resolve the problem of double taxation.
Businessmen from both countries said long distances, scattered shipments and poor communications were bottlenecks retarding the growth of bilateral trade.
Both Indian government and busines houses have had a long-standing preference for trade with English-speaking nations, which has also deterred ties with Latin America.
These countries account for just one percent of India's total foreign trade. The bulk is accounted for by three countries -- Argentina, Brazil and Mexico, Ramaiah said.
They have a 48 percent share of India's total trade with Latin America.
Ramaiah urged governments on both sides to provide business with more direct shipping facilities and improved communications to ease the movement of goods.
Delhi also intends to use warming ties with South Africa, the geographical mid-point between India and Latin America, to improve trade channels, officials said.
